name: Riju Raveendran
forbes_bio: Riju Raveendran is the younger brother of edtech billionaire Byju Raveendran, the cofounder of learning app Byju's.
He has been associated with the company since its start in 2011 and now oversees administration and operations.
Riju has a small but valuable stake in Byju's parent company Think & Learn, which was valued at $22 billion in its March 2022 founding round.
Byju's went on an acquisition spree in 2021, spending more than $2 billion.
He loves playing tennis and football.

name: Bruce Mathieson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Bruce Mathieson operates his poker machine and pub empire Australian Liquor and Hospitality in a joint venture with supermarket giant Woolworths.
Mathieson is now a minority shareholder in the listed Endeavour Group, which holds both the Australian Liquor assets and Woolworth's extensive liquor retailing business.
In a board shakeup in 2024, Endeavour's chairman resigned as well as Mathieson's son, Bruce Mathieson Jr., who had a board seat.
He has a fondness for racehorses and part-owned a horse that ran in the Melbourne Cup.
He is battling a rare form of blood cancer.
forbes_facts: Bruce Mathieson has partnered with U.S. gambling giant Bally's to rescue financially-challenged Australian casino operator, The Star Entertainment Group.

name: Nguyen Dang Quang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Nguyen Dang Quang invested in commercial bank Techcombank in 1993 and later founded Masan Group with business partner, Ho Hung Anh, in 2004.
Masan Group has interests in a wide range of consumer and food product businesses, ranging from animal feeds to food processing.
While Ho Hung Anh, who is chairman of Techcombank, is in charge of the bank, Nguyen is focused on building Masan Group as its chairman.
In 2023, Bain Capital led a $500 million funding round in Masan, the global private equity giant's first-ever investment in Vietnam.

Techcom Securities, the brokerage arm of Techcombank, went public on the Ho Chi Minh City Stock Exchange in October 2025. Masan Consumer, the group's consumer goods unit, listed on the bourse two months later.
forbes_facts: Nguyen Dang Quang belongs to the wave of Vietnamese students who studied in Russia and Eastern Europe in the 1980s, after the Vietnam War.
He returned to Vietnam and worked for Vietnam's Academy of Sciences before joining the private sector in the 1990s.

name: Mehmet Kazanci
forbes_bio: Mehmet Kazanci is a shareholder of family-owned Kazancı Holding, one of Turkey's largest energy companies.
The $3.6 billion (revenue) company operates across the energy industry, including electricity generation and distribution, natural gas distribution and generator production.
Kazanci started the energy business in 1968 with the Watt Electric Motor Factory.
Kazancı Holding expanded its tourism business in the city of Bodrum, in 2022, with the 5-star Mirada Exclusive Hotel. It currently owns four hotels.

name: Rick Jackson
forbes_bio: Rick Jackson founded Jackson Healthcare, a healthcare staffing and services company. He is the 2026 Republican nominee for governor of Georgia.
Jackson's father abandoned the family when he was 9 months old. His mother was an alcoholic with a 6th-grade education who worked as a cocktail waitress.
He grew up in Techwood Homes, a public housing project near the campus of Georgia Tech where he got his start selling newspapers, peanuts and scalping tickets to football games.

Jackson began building and buying healthcare companies in the 1970s and united them into Jackson Healthcare in 2000. It now generates $3 billion in revenue from 22 businesses, focused on healthcare staffing.
In 2020, Jackson bought the only amoxicillin antibiotics plant in the U.S., in Bristol, Tennessee, out of bankruptcy and relaunched it as USAntibiotics.

Foreign nurses brought to work in the U.S. have filed suit in federal court alleging that a Jackson company violated labor laws and engaged in a racketeering conspiracy by promising nurses "the American dream," then locking them into predatory stay-or-pay contracts. Jackson has denied the claims.

name: Warren Kanders
sec_insider_companies: Cadre Holdings, Inc. (CDRE) - CEO AND CHAIRMAN; Clarus Corp (CLAR) - Executive Chairman
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Hurun Global (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Warren Kanders is the chairman and CEO of Jacksonville, Florida-based Cadre Holdings, which makes equipment for defense, law enforcement and nuclear safety.
In 1996, Kanders started buying up defense businesses with Robert Schiller and formed Armor Holdings. The pair sold the firm to BAE Systems for $4.5 billion in 2007.
In 2012, Kanders bought back some of those businesses, collectively known as Safariland, for $124 million alongside Safariland's management team.
He later reorganized Safariland and other defense and law enforcement suppliers under Cadre Holdings and took it public in 2021; he owns 28% of the firm.
In 2024, he bought L3Harris' antenna and test equipment business for $200 million and formed defense products manufacturer Fisica.
forbes_facts: Kanders served on the board of the Whitney Museum of American Art from 2006 to 2019, when he stepped down after protests amid Safariland's sales of tear gas.
Kanders owns stakes in outdoor equipment and apparel brands Clarus Corp, Mountain Khakis and Carve Designs.

name: Takao Kobayashi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2021); Hurun Global (2018-2021)
forbes_bio: Takao Kobayashi runs listed Japanese cosmetics manufacturer and retailer Kose Corp. with his brothers Kazutosh and Masanori Kobayashi.
Their grandfather, Kozaburo, started the company in 1946.
The three brothers inherited a minority stake each in the company.
Kose exports its products to Hong Kong, China, Singapore and Malaysia.

name: Shirou Terashita
forbes_bio: Shirou Terashita is president and CEO  of investor and shareholder relations firm IR Japan Holdings.
He joined the firm in 1982, eventually conducting a management buyout in 2008.
It was listed on Tokyo's JASDAQ bourse in 2011 and moved to the Tokyo Stock Exchange in 2018.
The company posted nearly $75 million in revenue in the fiscal year ended in March 2020 and about $24 million in net profit.
IR Japan has advised Japanese companies in proxy fights with activist investors.
